extraction.body: President Donald Trump announced a new "Super Intelligence Force" in a post on Truth Social Sunday, just days after signing an executive order renaming Artificial Intelligence. Trump says the force will "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," by coordinating the federal government's efforts. "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies," Trump said on Truth Social. He said the force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor will all serve as vice chairs. Clayton spoke with The Wall Street Journal about the force, saying, "The president asked that a group be put together." He said the panel has been tasked with reporting on the risks and opportunities AI poses within 120 days, and emphasized the U.S. government's desire to lead the industry, saying "the risk of not being first is high." According to The Journal, the force will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms, checking them for breaches, hacks and other incidents and issues. The Journal says in addition to Clayton and the vice chairs, Super Intelligence Force members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Super Intelligence vs AI The force is just the latest effort Trump has made, using the term superintelligence rather than artificial intelligence. During a UN General Assembly meeting last month, Trump said the word artificial "makes it sound fake, and it is not fake, it's actually amazing." Since then, he's signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to officially rebrand AI as "super intelligence" in federal communications.

President Donald Trump announced the formation of the “Hyperintelligence Force,” led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, to ensure the United States remains at the forefront of the AI field globally. Trump said the Hyperintelligence Force will prepare a comprehensive 120-day report on the risks and opportunities presented by AI technologies, with a focus on boosting innovation and protecting competition. Trump said the Hyperintelligence Force will cooperate with the private sector to review the development of advanced models in AI, considering the importance of maintaining US leadership in this strategic area. Trump said the risks the new force aims to assess include potential breaches, attacks, and incidents related to AI technologies, given the growing reliance on these technologies across various sectors. Trump chose Jay Clayton, the Director of National Intelligence, to be the first “AI Czar” and to lead the new force, according to an official announcement published on the Truth Social platform. extraction.body: President Donald Trump announced a new "Super Intelligence Force" in a post on Truth Social Sunday, just days after signing an executive order renaming Artificial Intelligence. Trump says the force will "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," by coordinating the federal government's efforts. "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies," Trump said on Truth Social. He said the force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor will all serve as vice chairs. Clayton spoke with The Wall Street Journal about the force, saying, "The president asked that a group be put together." He said the panel has been tasked with reporting on the risks and opportunities AI poses within 120 days, and emphasized the U.S. government's desire to lead the industry, saying "the risk of not being first is high." According to The Journal, the force will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms, checking them for breaches, hacks and other incidents and issues. The Journal says in addition to Clayton and the vice chairs, Super Intelligence Force members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Super Intelligence vs AI The force is just the latest effort Trump has made, using the term superintelligence rather than artificial intelligence. During a UN General Assembly meeting last month, Trump said the word artificial "makes it sound fake, and it is not fake, it's actually amazing." Since then, he's signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to officially rebrand AI as "super intelligence" in federal communications.

Clayton spoke with The Wall Street Journal about the force, saying, "The president asked that a group be put together." He said the panel has been tasked with reporting on the risks and opportunities AI poses within 120 days, and emphasized the U.S. government's desire to lead the industry, saying "the risk of not being first is high." According to The Journal, the force will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms, checking them for breaches, hacks and other incidents and issues.

The Journal says in addition to Clayton and the vice chairs, Super Intelligence Force members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles.
Super Intelligence vs AI The force is just the latest effort Trump has made, using the term superintelligence rather than artificial intelligence.

During a UN General Assembly meeting last month, Trump said the word artificial "makes it sound fake, and it is not fake, it's actually amazing." Since then, he's signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to officially rebrand AI as "super intelligence" in federal communications.

President Donald Trump announced the formation of the “Hyperintelligence Force,” led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, to ensure the United States remains at the forefront of the AI field globally. Trump said the Hyperintelligence Force will prepare a comprehensive 120-day report on the risks and opportunities presented by AI technologies, with a focus on boosting innovation and protecting competition. Trump said the Hyperintelligence Force will cooperate with the private sector to review the development of advanced models in AI, considering the importance of maintaining US leadership in this strategic area. Trump said the risks the new force aims to assess include potential breaches, attacks, and incidents related to AI technologies, given the growing reliance on these technologies across various sectors. Trump chose Jay Clayton, the Director of National Intelligence, to be the first “AI Czar” and to lead the new force, according to an official announcement published on the Truth Social platform. Andrew Ferguson, President of the Federal Trade Commission, and Emile Michael, Deputy Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering and the chief technology officer of the department, would join Clayton in managing the team. Scott Kobor, Director of the Office of Personnel Management, would also join the team, and it would file reports and recommendations directly to President Trump and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Trump formally announced the creation of what he called a “Super Intelligence Force,” and Trump wrote that it is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence. Clayton told The Wall Street Journal that “The risk of not being first is high,” and he said “Not being first increases the identified, and unidentified, risks, particularly from our adversaries.” Clayton said of the AI task force, “I expect there will be mechanisms developed in dialogue, just like there are in other industries.” The task force will have 120 days to prepare its findings and will examine existing laws and potential steps Congress could take while working with the technology industry to identify risks and opportunities. The charter calls for developing plans to respond to threats posed by advanced AI, while avoiding regulations that could hinder innovation and competition, and it said the task force will also review how breaches, hacks, model jailbreaks and other AI-related incidents are reported to the government. Task force has 120 days to research and report . Reported by CNBC . ABC13 Houston stresses the task force lacks details, while CNN emphasises concrete rogue-agent hacking incidents as the backdrop. extraction.body: What’s next from Apple? Well, you probably already got the memo that the iPhone 17 is coming. And if history is anything to go by, then new iPhones certainly won't be the only new products announced at the “Awe dropping” event in Cupertino, California, on September 9. So without further ado, here's everything we think Apple will launch next week. Let’s start with the obvious headliner. Apple is expected to shake things up a bit; instead of two standard and two Pro-branded models, Apple is expected to ditch the iPhone 17 Plus from this year's lineup and replace it with a new ultra-thin model , tentatively named “iPhone Air.” It should be around 5.5mm thick, except for the area with a pill-shaped horizontal bump for the single rear camera, and much lighter to hold in your hand. If true, that would make the iPhone Air over 2mm thinner than the iPhone 16 (which is 7.8 mm thick) but also the thinnest iPhone to date. It won't, however, file as the thinnest Apple product ever—that crown belongs to the 13-inch model of the 2024 iPad Pro, which is just 5.1 mm thick. The iPhone Air is also expected to be equipped with a 6.6-inch OLED always-on display (with 120Hz ProMotion refresh rates support) and have average battery life due to a smaller battery, because of constrained space inside the device. However, iOS 26's Apple Intelligence-powered battery optimization could mitigate battery compromises. Other rumored iPhone Air features include Apple's C1 modem, MagSafe charging, Camera Control and Action buttons, eSIM, and a starting price of $899—the same as the current ‌iPhone 16‌ Plus. The device should be available in black, white, light gold, and light blue color. As for the second-generation “e” iPhone, we're expecting the iPhone 17e to join Apple's 2025 smartphone lineup in spring 2026. The rest of the lineup should include the base iPhone 17 , along with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max models. All devices are said to feature a redesigned camera bump out the back, shaped like a pill and running across the full width of the device, similar to Google's Pixel phones. The telephoto camera on some of these phones may be upgraded to 48MP, with 8x optical zoom instead of 5x. Apple may also add support for lanyards and introduce a new "TechWoven" eco-friendly material for cases to replace the discontinued FineWoven fabric that no one liked. The regular iPhone 17 is said to include the classic black and white color options, in addition to four new choices—green, purple, steel gray (a version of space gray), and light blue, which is said to be similar to the Sierra Blue colorway of the iPhone 13 Pro but much brighter and more refined. On the other hand, the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max should be available to purchase in five color finishes: black, white, gray, orange, and dark blue. 2025 could be another year of stagnation for the Apple Watch Series 11 family due to same old design. In fact, supply chain publication DigiTimes recently said that a “significant redesign” is coming with a high-end Apple Watch model in 2026. Macworld discovered solid evidence that Touch ID biometric authentication is in the works for 2026's Apple Watch lineup. Meanwhile, the upcoming Apple S11 chip powering this year's Apple Watch lineup won't bring much of a performance jump. This claim is based on Apple's leaked code discovered by MacRumors , suggesting the S11 has the same T8310 microarchitecture as the previous two chips in the Apple Watch Series 10 and Series 9 models . These smartwatches could have 5G cellular connectivity instead of the existing LTE options, thanks to Mediatek's 5G RedCap technology designed for wearable devices that don't need standard 5G speeds. The third-generation ‌Apple Watch SE‌ may come in 1.6-inch and 1.8-inch display sizes, slightly bigger than the existing 1.57-inch and 1.78-inch screens. It could also have a Series 7-style thinner chassis with skinnier bezels, plus the S11 chip (vs. the S8 in the current model), bringing a notable performance jump and previously unsupported features like the double-tap gesture and more storage. Other possible upgrades include faster inductive charging, enhanced water resistance, and improved battery life. There are no rumors to suggest that the Apple Watch SE 3 will get missing features such as an always-on display, blood oxygen monitoring, or the ECG app. On top of that, we may also get an updated Ultra model. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 should also run the S11 chip and feature a higher-resolution LTPO3 OLED display (422 x 514 pixels instead of a 410 x 502 display in the Apple Watch Ultra 2), marking the biggest Apple Watch display to date. The biggest change expected is apparently satellite connectivity for the Emergency SOS features in areas without cellular or Wi-Fi coverage. If all this comes to pass, 2025 will mark the first time all three Apple Watch lines have been refreshed at the same time. The original AirPods started as an iPhone accessory, and Apple has unveiled several models of AirPods at iPhone events thus far. The current AirPods Pro 2 originally debuted in September 2022, and a USB-C version arrived a year later. After three years without an update in sight, the AirPods Pro are ripe for a decent hardware refresh. These earbuds could be the first to rock an updated Apple headphone chip. The current one is called H2 and supports Bluetooth 5.3, but it's unclear if a new version might bring Bluetooth 5.4 or 6.0. What seems certain are new computational audio features afforded by a faster chip, such as better active noise cancellation and improved adaptive audio. The charging case should be smaller, possibly matching that of the AirPods 4. It may borrow another feature from the AirPods 4: an invisible capacitive touch surface instead of the physical pairing button. Like with the AirPods 4, you'd double-tap the front of the case just below the discreet status light when the lid is open to initiate Bluetooth pairing mode. Having a uniform charging case for the regular AirPods and the AirPods Pro would certainly make everyone's life easier, whether you sell cases for AirPods or are in the market for one. Existing AirPods Pro 2 owners will get new features by way of software when the iOS 26 update drops this fall, including auto-pause while sleeping, using AirPods as a camera remote , improved call quality, studio-quality audio recording, charging reminders, and others. The smaller charging case suggests that the earpieces will be redesigned, too. According to leaks, the AirPods Pro 3 should have a shorter stem with a bigger in-ear section sporting a more contoured appearance for an improved fit and comfort. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has called for in-ear sensors to measure heart rates (for fitness tracking without an Apple Watch) and body temperature, but these health features may have been delayed. The “Awe dropping” event may also give us a new HomePod mini speaker as an official successor to the original HomePod mini . Released in November 2020, the HomePod mini is powered by the Apple Watch Series 5 chip, called the Apple S5, from 2019. The second-generation upgrade should bring a new chip based on the processor in last year's Apple Watch Series 11, but sporting a 4-core Neural Engine and a faster dual-core CPU based on the Apple A16 (a 2022-era Apple chip which first appeared in the iPhone 14 Pros. The Neural Engine is used for AI tasks, so this could be the first HomePod speaker to support on-device Apple Intelligence features like the upcoming Siri AI refresh and on-device Siri processing. Other rumored capabilities and features for the HomePod mini 2 are thought to include an in-house designed Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip with Wi-Fi 6E support (code-named “Proxima”) replacing Qualcomm silicon, along with new color options. Apple doesn't refresh the Apple TV annually. The third-generation model was released in 2022, and even though it's still a capable streaming device, its CPU is starting to show age—especially with the redesigned Liquid Glass user interface that only works on the third-generation Apple TV 4K. A simple spec bump could solve that in one fell swoop. To that end, some folks have been keeping their fingers crossed for a refreshed Apple TV 4K powered by an Apple Intelligence-enabled A17 Pro chip. Compared to the A15 Bionic in the current Apple TV 4K, the A17 Pro would bring faster performance for streaming, apps, and gaming (especially with its GPU supporting hardware-accelerated ray tracing). The A17 Pro may also bring Apple Intelligence to the biggest screen in your house. While most of the existing Apple Intelligence features would make a poor fit for a streaming device, the next Apple TV will surely benefit from Apple's revamped, AI-infused Siri when it finally arrives later in 2026. The device is also said to use Apple's upcoming combo Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip for more reliable streaming and Continuity features . Another prediction for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K is a built-in camera for FaceTime videoconferencing and gesture-based controls. This rumor was first started by Mark Gurman at Bloomberg , who said this technology will work “seamlessly with both the iPhone and Vision Pro.” However, no credible source has corroborated Gurman's reporting. On the other hand, tvOS 26 brings support for FaceTime audio and phone call notifications on the Apple TV screen, suggesting a camera-enabled Apple TV could be coming after all. The current Apple TVs support FaceTime video calls, but you need a clunky attachment to mount your iPhone at the top of your TV set to make the most of the Continuity Camera functionality. Also, the need for an additional accessory probably means that not many people use FaceTime on their Apple TV. A camera-enabled model could change that. Announcements we don't expect at the “Awe dropping” event include Mac laptops and desktops powered by next-generation Apple M5 chips, along with updated iPad Air and budget iPad models, and an upgraded Studio Display with mini-LED technology instead of LCD. Wild cards like the AirPods Max 2, an iPhone 17e, an M5-powered iPad Pro, or M5 Vision Pro are also out of the question for September. However, any of those expected products could make an appearance at a Mac-focused event that Apple should hold in October. We want to hear from you. passages: What’s next from Apple? Well, you probably already got the memo that the iPhone 17 is coming. And if history is anything to go by, then new iPhones certainly won't be the only new products announced at the “Awe dropping” event in Cupertino, California, on September 9. So without further ado, here's everything we think Apple will launch next week.

Let’s start with the obvious headliner. Apple is expected to shake things up a bit; instead of two standard and two Pro-branded models, Apple is expected to ditch the iPhone 17 Plus from this year's lineup and replace it with a new ultra-thin model , tentatively named “iPhone Air.”

It should be around 5.5mm thick, except for the area with a pill-shaped horizontal bump for the single rear camera, and much lighter to hold in your hand. If true, that would make the iPhone Air over 2mm thinner than the iPhone 16 (which is 7.8 mm thick) but also the thinnest iPhone to date. It won't, however, file as the thinnest Apple product ever—that crown belongs to the 13-inch model of the 2024 iPad Pro, which is just 5.1 mm thick.

The iPhone Air is also expected to be equipped with a 6.6-inch OLED always-on display (with 120Hz ProMotion refresh rates support) and have average battery life due to a smaller battery, because of constrained space inside the device. However, iOS 26's Apple Intelligence-powered battery optimization could mitigate battery compromises.

Other rumored iPhone Air features include Apple's C1 modem, MagSafe charging, Camera Control and Action buttons, eSIM, and a starting price of $899—the same as the current ‌iPhone 16‌ Plus. The device should be available in black, white, light gold, and light blue color.
As for the second-generation “e” iPhone, we're expecting the iPhone 17e to join Apple's 2025 smartphone lineup in spring 2026.

The rest of the lineup should include the base iPhone 17 , along with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max models. All devices are said to feature a redesigned camera bump out the back, shaped like a pill and running across the full width of the device, similar to Google's Pixel phones. The telephoto camera on some of these phones may be upgraded to 48MP, with 8x optical zoom instead of 5x.

Apple may also add support for lanyards and introduce a new "TechWoven" eco-friendly material for cases to replace the discontinued FineWoven fabric that no one liked. The regular iPhone 17 is said to include the classic black and white color options, in addition to four new choices—green, purple, steel gray (a version of space gray), and light blue, which is said to be similar to the Sierra Blue colorway of the iPhone 13 Pro but much brighter and more refined.
On the other hand, the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max should be available to purchase in five color finishes: black, white, gray, orange, and dark blue.

2025 could be another year of stagnation for the Apple Watch Series 11 family due to same old design. In fact, supply chain publication DigiTimes recently said that a “significant redesign” is coming with a high-end Apple Watch model in 2026. Macworld discovered solid evidence that Touch ID biometric authentication is in the works for 2026's Apple Watch lineup.

Meanwhile, the upcoming Apple S11 chip powering this year's Apple Watch lineup won't bring much of a performance jump. This claim is based on Apple's leaked code discovered by MacRumors , suggesting the S11 has the same T8310 microarchitecture as the previous two chips in the Apple Watch Series 10 and Series 9 models . These smartwatches could have 5G cellular connectivity instead of the existing LTE options, thanks to Mediatek's 5G RedCap technology designed for wearable devices that don't need standard 5G speeds.

The third-generation ‌Apple Watch SE‌ may come in 1.6-inch and 1.8-inch display sizes, slightly bigger than the existing 1.57-inch and 1.78-inch screens. It could also have a Series 7-style thinner chassis with skinnier bezels, plus the S11 chip (vs. the S8 in the current model), bringing a notable performance jump and previously unsupported features like the double-tap gesture and more storage. Other possible upgrades include faster inductive charging, enhanced water resistance, and improved battery life.
There are no rumors to suggest that the Apple Watch SE 3 will get missing features such as an always-on display, blood oxygen monitoring, or the ECG app.

On top of that, we may also get an updated Ultra model. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 should also run the S11 chip and feature a higher-resolution LTPO3 OLED display (422 x 514 pixels instead of a 410 x 502 display in the Apple Watch Ultra 2), marking the biggest Apple Watch display to date. The biggest change expected is apparently satellite connectivity for the Emergency SOS features in areas without cellular or Wi-Fi coverage. If all this comes to pass, 2025 will mark the first time all three Apple Watch lines have been refreshed at the same time.

The original AirPods started as an iPhone accessory, and Apple has unveiled several models of AirPods at iPhone events thus far. The current AirPods Pro 2 originally debuted in September 2022, and a USB-C version arrived a year later. After three years without an update in sight, the AirPods Pro are ripe for a decent hardware refresh.

These earbuds could be the first to rock an updated Apple headphone chip. The current one is called H2 and supports Bluetooth 5.3, but it's unclear if a new version might bring Bluetooth 5.4 or 6.0. What seems certain are new computational audio features afforded by a faster chip, such as better active noise cancellation and improved adaptive audio.

The charging case should be smaller, possibly matching that of the AirPods 4. It may borrow another feature from the AirPods 4: an invisible capacitive touch surface instead of the physical pairing button. Like with the AirPods 4, you'd double-tap the front of the case just below the discreet status light when the lid is open to initiate Bluetooth pairing mode. Having a uniform charging case for the regular AirPods and the AirPods Pro would certainly make everyone's life easier, whether you sell cases for AirPods or are in the market for one.

Existing AirPods Pro 2 owners will get new features by way of software when the iOS 26 update drops this fall, including auto-pause while sleeping, using AirPods as a camera remote , improved call quality, studio-quality audio recording, charging reminders, and others.

The smaller charging case suggests that the earpieces will be redesigned, too. According to leaks, the AirPods Pro 3 should have a shorter stem with a bigger in-ear section sporting a more contoured appearance for an improved fit and comfort. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has called for in-ear sensors to measure heart rates (for fitness tracking without an Apple Watch) and body temperature, but these health features may have been delayed.

The “Awe dropping” event may also give us a new HomePod mini speaker as an official successor to the original HomePod mini . Released in November 2020, the HomePod mini is powered by the Apple Watch Series 5 chip, called the Apple S5, from 2019.

The second-generation upgrade should bring a new chip based on the processor in last year's Apple Watch Series 11, but sporting a 4-core Neural Engine and a faster dual-core CPU based on the Apple A16 (a 2022-era Apple chip which first appeared in the iPhone 14 Pros.
The Neural Engine is used for AI tasks, so this could be the first HomePod speaker to support on-device Apple Intelligence features like the upcoming Siri AI refresh and on-device Siri processing.

Other rumored capabilities and features for the HomePod mini 2 are thought to include an in-house designed Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip with Wi-Fi 6E support (code-named “Proxima”) replacing Qualcomm silicon, along with new color options.

Apple doesn't refresh the Apple TV annually. The third-generation model was released in 2022, and even though it's still a capable streaming device, its CPU is starting to show age—especially with the redesigned Liquid Glass user interface that only works on the third-generation Apple TV 4K. A simple spec bump could solve that in one fell swoop.

To that end, some folks have been keeping their fingers crossed for a refreshed Apple TV 4K powered by an Apple Intelligence-enabled A17 Pro chip. Compared to the A15 Bionic in the current Apple TV 4K, the A17 Pro would bring faster performance for streaming, apps, and gaming (especially with its GPU supporting hardware-accelerated ray tracing).

The A17 Pro may also bring Apple Intelligence to the biggest screen in your house. While most of the existing Apple Intelligence features would make a poor fit for a streaming device, the next Apple TV will surely benefit from Apple's revamped, AI-infused Siri when it finally arrives later in 2026. The device is also said to use Apple's upcoming combo Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip for more reliable streaming and Continuity features .

Another prediction for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K is a built-in camera for FaceTime videoconferencing and gesture-based controls. This rumor was first started by Mark Gurman at Bloomberg , who said this technology will work “seamlessly with both the iPhone and Vision Pro.” However, no credible source has corroborated Gurman's reporting. On the other hand, tvOS 26 brings support for FaceTime audio and phone call notifications on the Apple TV screen, suggesting a camera-enabled Apple TV could be coming after all.

The current Apple TVs support FaceTime video calls, but you need a clunky attachment to mount your iPhone at the top of your TV set to make the most of the Continuity Camera functionality. Also, the need for an additional accessory probably means that not many people use FaceTime on their Apple TV. A camera-enabled model could change that.

Announcements we don't expect at the “Awe dropping” event include Mac laptops and desktops powered by next-generation Apple M5 chips, along with updated iPad Air and budget iPad models, and an upgraded Studio Display with mini-LED technology instead of LCD.

Wild cards like the AirPods Max 2, an iPhone 17e, an M5-powered iPad Pro, or M5 Vision Pro are also out of the question for September. However, any of those expected products could make an appearance at a Mac-focused event that Apple should hold in October.

extraction.body: Apple has confirmed that it will begin unveiling new products from Monday, March 2. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), Apple CEO Tim Cook wrote, “A big week ahead. It all starts Monday morning!” He followed this with the hashtag #AppleLaunch, indicating that multiple announcements could be lined up leading up to Apple’s event on March 4. Apple has not officially detailed what it plans to introduce, but reports suggest several products are nearing launch. These include the iPhone 17e, higher-end MacBook Pro variants, and a MacBook Air powered by the M5 chip. In addition, speculation points to entirely new hardware, such as a more affordable MacBook that could run on an iPhone-class processor instead of the usual M-series silicon.A big week ahead. It all starts Monday morning! #AppleLaunch pic.twitter.com/PQ9gM2Gl2r— Tim Cook (@tim_cook) February 26, 2026Apple March 4 “Special Experience” event: What to expectAccording to a report by 9To5Mac, Apple’s March 4 event will be invite-only, with media gatherings expected in cities including New York, London and Shanghai. Instead, Apple is likely to make product announcements online across the week. Here is a closer look at the devices that could be introduced: iPhone 17e The iPhone 17e is expected to continue Apple’s strategy of equipping its more affordable iPhones with up-to-date internals. After the iPhone 16e adopted the A18 chip, the upcoming model is likely to move to the A19 processor, which debuted with the iPhone 17 lineup. This could bring improvements to overall performance, graphics processing and neural engine capabilities. A report by Macotakara suggests the device may also feature Apple’s newer C1X modem, which is said to offer faster speeds than the C1 modem used in the iPhone 16e. It could also include Apple’s in-house N1 networking chip to handle Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Thread connectivity.ALSO READ: Apple likely to produce 30% of iPhones in India in a few yearsDesign-wise, the iPhone 17e is expected to retain its current look, including a notch instead of the Dynamic Island and a single rear camera. It is still expected to use a 60Hz panel, without ProMotion or an always-on display. Camera updates could include an 18MP Centre Stage front camera for improved framing during video calls, while the rear camera may remain a single 48MP sensor. MagSafe support is also expected to be added. MacBook Pro with M5 Pro, M5 Max Apple introduced a 14-inch MacBook Pro with the standard M5 chip in October, but did not launch the higher-tier Pro and Max versions at the time. The company is now expected to round out the lineup with MacBook Pro models powered by the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, and 16-inch display. Apart from the anticipated performance improvements delivered by the new chips, no significant design changes or additional hardware upgrades are currently expected. Low-cost MacBook Apple could also introduce a new entry-level MacBook that uses an iPhone-grade A-series processor instead of an M-series chip. Reports indicate it may run on the A18 Pro chip, with performance said to approach that of M1-based MacBooks in certain workloads. The device could feature a smaller 12.9-inch display with lower brightness than the display on the MacBook Air. The new low-cost MacBook could get either an aluminium or plastic chassis. Apple may also expand the colour palette beyond the traditional silver and grey finishes.ALSO READ: Apple's low-cost MacBook may skip premium features from MacBook Air: ReportM5 MacBook Air A refreshed MacBook Air powered by the standard M5 chip is also anticipated. However, the 2026 MacBook Air may incorporate Apple’s N1 networking chip, which could improve wireless performance and connectivity. M5 Mac Studio Apple is reportedly preparing an update to the Mac Studio. The current version runs on M4 Max and M3 Ultra chips, and the next iteration is expected to transition to M5 Max and M5 Ultra variants. Base iPad (11th generation) The 11th-generation entry-level iPad is also expected to debut next week. While the overall design may remain similar, the device could receive a substantial performance boost through the A18 chip, potentially enabling Apple Intelligence features. It may also introduce Apple’s in-house modem for Wi-Fi and 5G connectivity. Other devicesApple Studio Display 2: Apple is reportedly working on two new Studio Display models featuring mini-LED panels in 27-inch and 32-inch sizes. The larger version could offer an upgraded 6K resolution display. These monitors may be powered by the A19 Pro chip rather than the older A13 Bionic.New Apple TV 4K: The next-generation Apple TV 4K could run on either the A18 or A17 Pro chip, enabling support for Apple Intelligence capabilities. It is also expected to feature a built-in camera for FaceTime. The device may adopt Apple’s N1 networking chip, supporting Wi-Fi 7 and improved wireless connectivity.HomePod mini 2: The second-generation HomePod mini could include a newer S-series processor, such as the S9 or S10, which may enhance performance and unlock select Apple Intelligence features. Like the anticipated Apple TV 4K, it may integrate the N1 networking chip for improved stability and faster Wi-Fi 7 speeds.

extraction.body: What’s next from Apple? Well, you probably already got the memo that the iPhone 17 is coming. And if history is anything to go by, then new iPhones certainly won't be the only new products announced at the “Awe dropping” event in Cupertino, California, on September 9. So without further ado, here's everything we think Apple will launch next week. Let’s start with the obvious headliner. Apple is expected to shake things up a bit; instead of two standard and two Pro-branded models, Apple is expected to ditch the iPhone 17 Plus from this year's lineup and replace it with a new ultra-thin model , tentatively named “iPhone Air.” It should be around 5.5mm thick, except for the area with a pill-shaped horizontal bump for the single rear camera, and much lighter to hold in your hand. If true, that would make the iPhone Air over 2mm thinner than the iPhone 16 (which is 7.8 mm thick) but also the thinnest iPhone to date. It won't, however, file as the thinnest Apple product ever—that crown belongs to the 13-inch model of the 2024 iPad Pro, which is just 5.1 mm thick. The iPhone Air is also expected to be equipped with a 6.6-inch OLED always-on display (with 120Hz ProMotion refresh rates support) and have average battery life due to a smaller battery, because of constrained space inside the device. However, iOS 26's Apple Intelligence-powered battery optimization could mitigate battery compromises. Other rumored iPhone Air features include Apple's C1 modem, MagSafe charging, Camera Control and Action buttons, eSIM, and a starting price of $899—the same as the current ‌iPhone 16‌ Plus. The device should be available in black, white, light gold, and light blue color. As for the second-generation “e” iPhone, we're expecting the iPhone 17e to join Apple's 2025 smartphone lineup in spring 2026. The rest of the lineup should include the base iPhone 17 , along with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max models. All devices are said to feature a redesigned camera bump out the back, shaped like a pill and running across the full width of the device, similar to Google's Pixel phones. The telephoto camera on some of these phones may be upgraded to 48MP, with 8x optical zoom instead of 5x. Apple may also add support for lanyards and introduce a new "TechWoven" eco-friendly material for cases to replace the discontinued FineWoven fabric that no one liked. The regular iPhone 17 is said to include the classic black and white color options, in addition to four new choices—green, purple, steel gray (a version of space gray), and light blue, which is said to be similar to the Sierra Blue colorway of the iPhone 13 Pro but much brighter and more refined. On the other hand, the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max should be available to purchase in five color finishes: black, white, gray, orange, and dark blue. 2025 could be another year of stagnation for the Apple Watch Series 11 family due to same old design. In fact, supply chain publication DigiTimes recently said that a “significant redesign” is coming with a high-end Apple Watch model in 2026. Macworld discovered solid evidence that Touch ID biometric authentication is in the works for 2026's Apple Watch lineup. Meanwhile, the upcoming Apple S11 chip powering this year's Apple Watch lineup won't bring much of a performance jump. This claim is based on Apple's leaked code discovered by MacRumors , suggesting the S11 has the same T8310 microarchitecture as the previous two chips in the Apple Watch Series 10 and Series 9 models . These smartwatches could have 5G cellular connectivity instead of the existing LTE options, thanks to Mediatek's 5G RedCap technology designed for wearable devices that don't need standard 5G speeds. The third-generation ‌Apple Watch SE‌ may come in 1.6-inch and 1.8-inch display sizes, slightly bigger than the existing 1.57-inch and 1.78-inch screens. It could also have a Series 7-style thinner chassis with skinnier bezels, plus the S11 chip (vs. the S8 in the current model), bringing a notable performance jump and previously unsupported features like the double-tap gesture and more storage. Other possible upgrades include faster inductive charging, enhanced water resistance, and improved battery life. There are no rumors to suggest that the Apple Watch SE 3 will get missing features such as an always-on display, blood oxygen monitoring, or the ECG app. On top of that, we may also get an updated Ultra model. The Apple Watch Ultra 3 should also run the S11 chip and feature a higher-resolution LTPO3 OLED display (422 x 514 pixels instead of a 410 x 502 display in the Apple Watch Ultra 2), marking the biggest Apple Watch display to date. The biggest change expected is apparently satellite connectivity for the Emergency SOS features in areas without cellular or Wi-Fi coverage. If all this comes to pass, 2025 will mark the first time all three Apple Watch lines have been refreshed at the same time. The original AirPods started as an iPhone accessory, and Apple has unveiled several models of AirPods at iPhone events thus far. The current AirPods Pro 2 originally debuted in September 2022, and a USB-C version arrived a year later. After three years without an update in sight, the AirPods Pro are ripe for a decent hardware refresh. These earbuds could be the first to rock an updated Apple headphone chip. The current one is called H2 and supports Bluetooth 5.3, but it's unclear if a new version might bring Bluetooth 5.4 or 6.0. What seems certain are new computational audio features afforded by a faster chip, such as better active noise cancellation and improved adaptive audio. The charging case should be smaller, possibly matching that of the AirPods 4. It may borrow another feature from the AirPods 4: an invisible capacitive touch surface instead of the physical pairing button. Like with the AirPods 4, you'd double-tap the front of the case just below the discreet status light when the lid is open to initiate Bluetooth pairing mode. Having a uniform charging case for the regular AirPods and the AirPods Pro would certainly make everyone's life easier, whether you sell cases for AirPods or are in the market for one. Existing AirPods Pro 2 owners will get new features by way of software when the iOS 26 update drops this fall, including auto-pause while sleeping, using AirPods as a camera remote , improved call quality, studio-quality audio recording, charging reminders, and others. The smaller charging case suggests that the earpieces will be redesigned, too. According to leaks, the AirPods Pro 3 should have a shorter stem with a bigger in-ear section sporting a more contoured appearance for an improved fit and comfort. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has called for in-ear sensors to measure heart rates (for fitness tracking without an Apple Watch) and body temperature, but these health features may have been delayed. The “Awe dropping” event may also give us a new HomePod mini speaker as an official successor to the original HomePod mini . Released in November 2020, the HomePod mini is powered by the Apple Watch Series 5 chip, called the Apple S5, from 2019. The second-generation upgrade should bring a new chip based on the processor in last year's Apple Watch Series 11, but sporting a 4-core Neural Engine and a faster dual-core CPU based on the Apple A16 (a 2022-era Apple chip which first appeared in the iPhone 14 Pros. The Neural Engine is used for AI tasks, so this could be the first HomePod speaker to support on-device Apple Intelligence features like the upcoming Siri AI refresh and on-device Siri processing. Other rumored capabilities and features for the HomePod mini 2 are thought to include an in-house designed Wi-Fi and Bluetooth combo chip with Wi-Fi 6E support (code-named “Proxima”) replacing Qualcomm silicon, along with new color options. Apple doesn't refresh the Apple TV annually. The third-generation model was released in 2022, and even though it's still a capable streaming device, its CPU is starting to show age—especially with the redesigned Liquid Glass user interface that only works on the third-generation Apple TV 4K. A simple spec bump could solve that in one fell swoop. To that end, some folks have been keeping their fingers crossed for a refreshed Apple TV 4K powered by an Apple Intelligence-enabled A17 Pro chip. Compared to the A15 Bionic in the current Apple TV 4K, the A17 Pro would bring faster performance for streaming, apps, and gaming (especially with its GPU supporting hardware-accelerated ray tracing). The A17 Pro may also bring Apple Intelligence to the biggest screen in your house. While most of the existing Apple Intelligence features would make a poor fit for a streaming device, the next Apple TV will surely benefit from Apple's revamped, AI-infused Siri when it finally arrives later in 2026. The device is also said to use Apple's upcoming combo Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip for more reliable streaming and Continuity features . Another prediction for the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K is a built-in camera for FaceTime videoconferencing and gesture-based controls. This rumor was first started by Mark Gurman at Bloomberg , who said this technology will work “seamlessly with both the iPhone and Vision Pro.” However, no credible source has corroborated Gurman's reporting. On the other hand, tvOS 26 brings support for FaceTime audio and phone call notifications on the Apple TV screen, suggesting a camera-enabled Apple TV could be coming after all. The current Apple TVs support FaceTime video calls, but you need a clunky attachment to mount your iPhone at the top of your TV set to make the most of the Continuity Camera functionality. Also, the need for an additional accessory probably means that not many people use FaceTime on their Apple TV. A camera-enabled model could change that. Announcements we don't expect at the “Awe dropping” event include Mac laptops and desktops powered by next-generation Apple M5 chips, along with updated iPad Air and budget iPad models, and an upgraded Studio Display with mini-LED technology instead of LCD. Wild cards like the AirPods Max 2, an iPhone 17e, an M5-powered iPad Pro, or M5 Vision Pro are also out of the question for September. However, any of those expected products could make an appearance at a Mac-focused event that Apple should hold in October. We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625 feet (5,067 metres) in just over 30 seconds. The United ⁠Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general has said the co-pilot had used a crash axe in the attempted “terrorist attack”, in which the pilot was stabbed mid-air. Numerous media outlets have named the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national. A source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014, before arriving in the country to commence a university course the following year. He left Australia in 2017, and his visa was cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed he was no longer enrolled in the course, the source said. The Australian federal police (AFP) on Sunday said multiple agencies – including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (Asio) – were probing the man’s connections to the country. “The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man’s links to Australia,” an AFP spokesperson said. “An update will be provided at an appropriate time.” US media outlets, including CNN, reported that a now-deleted LinkedIn profile said al-Hammami had studied engineering at an Australian university. Guardian Australia has not verified which university the co-pilot attended. It came after a British university, Buckinghamshire New University, said a student named Hamam al-Hammami had “previously completed a distance-learning course in aviation management” at the institution. It added: “He did not undertake any pilot training at the university.” A flydubai spokesperson on Saturday said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still ‌under investigation and the airline was not in a position to comment further. The airline’s flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv have been suspended until further notice after the attack. The Omani co-pilot and the flight’s Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, were taken to the UAE, as it leads the investigation. Officials have said a number of countries including Israel are participating. The Wall Street Journal has reported that the co-pilot had been barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views. He was then moved to an administrative job at Oman Air, according to the official, before being hired by the UAE-based budget airline flydubai.

Australian security agencies have launched an investigation after it emerged that the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound flight spent about two years in the country as a student.

Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625 feet (5,067 metres) in just over 30 seconds.

The United ⁠Arab Emirates’ prosecutor general has said the co-pilot had used a crash axe in the attempted “terrorist attack”, in which the pilot was stabbed mid-air. Numerous media outlets have named the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national.

A source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014, before arriving in the country to commence a university course the following year.
He left Australia in 2017, and his visa was cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed he was no longer enrolled in the course, the source said.
The Australian federal police (AFP) on Sunday said multiple agencies – including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (Asio) – were probing the man’s connections to the country.

sources.title: Flydubai Attack: Co-Pilot’s 2-Year Stay In Australia On Student Visa Under Security Scanner
passages: Australian security agencies have launched an investigation into the links of the flydubai co-pilot accused of attempting to hijack an Israel-bound passenger flight, after it emerged that he spent about two years in Australia as a student, The Guardian reported.

According to The Guardian, a source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014 before travelling to Australia the following year to begin a university course.
A reserve flydubai pilot crew travelling on the aircraft subsequently landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where Saudi authorities detained the co-pilot.

The probe comes as investigators in the UAE examine the circumstances, motives and background of the alleged mid-air attack on flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

extraction.body: Australian security agencies have launched an investigation into the links of the flydubai co-pilot accused of attempting to hijack an Israel-bound passenger flight, after it emerged that he spent about two years in Australia as a student, The Guardian reported. The probe comes as investigators in the UAE examine the circumstances, motives and background of the alleged mid-air attack on flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv. According to The Guardian, a source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014 before travelling to Australia the following year to begin a university course. He remained in the country until 2017, when he left Australia. The source said the man’s Australian student visa was subsequently cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed that he was no longer enrolled in the course. Australian Agencies Probe Links The Australian Federal Police (AFP) said on Sunday that multiple agencies, including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO), were investigating the co-pilot’s connections to Australia, according to The Guardian. The development adds an international dimension to an investigation already involving authorities in the UAE, Israel and Saudi Arabia. The alleged attack took place on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to take control of the aircraft. Passengers and crew members managed to subdue the co-pilot, averting what Israeli officials have described as an apparent attempt to crash the plane. A reserve flydubai pilot crew travelling on the aircraft subsequently landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where Saudi authorities detained the co-pilot. The co-pilot was transferred to the UAE on Thursday. Reuters reported, citing a source briefed on the investigation, that Israeli officials were expected to question him as part of the wider probe. An Israeli government official told Reuters that Israeli investigators would participate in the UAE-led investigation alongside Emirati authorities. Co-Pilot’s Motive Still Under Investigation The UAE has opened an investigation into the incident, with state media reporting that authorities were seeking to establish its circumstances and motives and determine whether it was linked to terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction. Flydubai Chief Executive Ghaith Al Ghaith said in his first public comments on the incident that an official investigation was underway with the airline’s support. “It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts,” Al Ghaith said in a written statement, while acknowledging that there were “many questions” surrounding what happened on flight FZ1073. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that Israel was investigating whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone’s direction.

extraction.body: TEL AVIV — Early indications suggest the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and trying to seize control of an Israel-bound plane acted alone, rather than as part of a larger organization or on behalf of a foreign government, multiple U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official told NBC News. The U.S. officials cautioned that the investigation into Wednesday’s midair attack remains at an early stage. “The assessment is that he operated alone. Right now, it looks like a case of ‘lone wolf’ terrorism inspired by content found online,” said Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official in the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency. “We still need to wait for the final investigation results to determine whether an organization or a state is behind it,” he added. Emirati authorities, who are leading the investigation, said Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash ax and attempted to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls in an attempted terrorist attack. The flight was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted when crew members and passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials. NBC News has identified the suspect as Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, based on information from multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East. Authorities have not released his identity. UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said Saturday that investigators were working to establish the incident’s “full circumstances, motives, and any links.” The preliminary assessment comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that investigators were examining whether the attacker had been sent by someone. President Donald Trump also raised the possibility of Iranian involvement Thursday, threatening renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack. A senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation previously told NBC News there were no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack. The flight captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar , said Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi that he had been severely injured and could sense the aircraft descending before he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene. “I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Raf Sanchez and Paul Goldman reported from Tel Aviv and Tom Winter from New York.

Authorities have identified the accused co-pilot as Hamam al Hammami, an Omani national who was born in the UAE and has a Syrian mother. (Photo: Social Media) Flydubai Attack Live Update: A routine international flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv has turned into a major security investigation after Australian authorities began examining the background and connections of the co-pilot accused of attacking the captain in the cockpit. Australian authorities confirmed that the Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team, involving the Australian Federal Police (AFP), Victoria Police and the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO), is investigating Hamam al Hammami’s "links to Australia". The Omani national reportedly studied in Melbourne, with local reports identifying RMIT University as the institution he attended. The investigation adds a new international dimension to the September 30 incident involving flydubai Flight 1073. The Boeing 737 was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv when al Hammami allegedly attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit. Australia has emerged as a key part of the investigation into flydubai co-pilot Hamam al Hammami after authorities confirmed they are examining his links to the country. The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team, which includes the Australian Federal Police, Victoria Police and ASIO, is looking into his time in Australia, including reports that he studied at RMIT University in Melbourne. Investigators are also examining allegations about his activities and possible extremist links while he was in the country. Authorities have identified the accused co-pilot as Hamam al Hammami, an Omani national who was born in the UAE and has a Syrian mother. Reports indicate that his background stretches across several countries. He reportedly studied in Melbourne before completing a distance-learning aviation management course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK. Australian media reports have also raised questions about his activities while he was in the country. The Financial Times reported that al Hammami allegedly visited radical mosques and extremist websites during his time in Australia, citing people familiar with the investigation. The report also said Australian intelligence agencies had previously held a file on him. Reuters said it could not independently verify those claims. "The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team (VIC JCTT), comprising the AFP, Victoria Police and ASIO, can confirm it is investigating the man's links to Australia. An update will be provided at an appropriate time," an Australian Federal Police spokesperson said. The flight left Dubai on Wednesday carrying 182 people and was heading toward Tel Aviv when the situation inside the cockpit suddenly escalated. According to UAE authorities, al Hammami attacked the captain using an emergency crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft. The incident sent the aircraft into a steep descent, with reports indicating that it dropped from around 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet in roughly a minute. Passengers and members of the crew eventually overpowered the co-pilot. The aircraft diverted to Saudi Arabia, where it made an emergency landing in Tabuk. Captain Smit Machchhar, who was injured during the attack, has since been praised for his actions. Reports say he managed to open the cockpit door despite his injuries, allowing others to intervene and help regain control of the aircraft. The UAE prosecutor general described the incident as a "terrorist attack" and said investigators were examining the circumstances, motive, possible connections and both physical and digital evidence. UAE senior diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash also described the incident as a "dangerous terrorist act" and praised the captain for preventing a much larger catastrophe. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu separately said the co-pilot had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination", adding that it appeared "very likely that he was going to down the plane". Authorities have not yet publicly established whether al Hammami acted alone or had support from an extremist organisation. A Gulf diplomat told the Associated Press that investigators were trying to determine whether he was a "lone wolf, or has any connection with any extremist groups". The investigation is also examining al Hammami's history before he joined flydubai. Sources cited by the Associated Press said Oman had previously banned him from flying because of concerns that he had adopted extremist views. That has raised questions about how he later obtained employment with a UAE-based airline and was assigned to an international passenger flight. The case has therefore expanded beyond the actions on Flight 1073. Investigators are now examining his education, travel history, online activity, previous aviation employment and any possible extremist connections. While investigators focus on the co-pilot, Captain Smit Machchhar has received widespread praise for his response during the attack. The Indian pilot fought to regain control of the cockpit after being attacked and helped create an opportunity for passengers and other crew members to intervene. He was later treated for his injuries. Israeli officials have praised Machchhar's actions, while reports said he was visited in hospital by senior UAE officials. The incident has also taken on a wider geopolitical dimension. US President Donald Trump said early information he had received suggested possible links between the attack and Iran. He warned that if Iranian agents were found responsible, the United States would "hit them very hard". No evidence establishing Iranian involvement has been publicly presented, and investigations into the incident remain underway. For now, Australian, Emirati and other authorities are focusing on reconstructing al Hammami's movements and background and determining whether the attack was the work of an individual or part of a wider extremist network.

The probe comes as investigators in the UAE examine the circumstances, motives and background of the alleged mid-air attack on flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying more than 170 passengers and crew from Dubai to Tel Aviv.

According to The Guardian, a source familiar with the case, but not authorised to speak publicly, said the man was granted an Australian student visa in 2014 before travelling to Australia the following year to begin a university course.
He remained in the country until 2017, when he left Australia.
The source said the man’s Australian student visa was subsequently cancelled in 2019 after authorities confirmed that he was no longer enrolled in the course.

Australian Agencies Probe Links The Australian Federal Police (AFP) said on Sunday that multiple agencies, including the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO), were investigating the co-pilot’s connections to Australia, according to The Guardian.
The development adds an international dimension to an investigation already involving authorities in the UAE, Israel and Saudi Arabia.
The alleged attack took place on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to take control of the aircraft.
Passengers and crew members managed to subdue the co-pilot, averting what Israeli officials have described as an apparent attempt to crash the plane.
A reserve flydubai pilot crew travelling on the aircraft subsequently landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where Saudi authorities detained the co-pilot.
The co-pilot was transferred to the UAE on Thursday.
Reuters reported, citing a source briefed on the investigation, that Israeli officials were expected to question him as part of the wider probe.
An Israeli government official told Reuters that Israeli investigators would participate in the UAE-led investigation alongside Emirati authorities.

Co-Pilot’s Motive Still Under Investigation The UAE has opened an investigation into the incident, with state media reporting that authorities were seeking to establish its circumstances and motives and determine whether it was linked to terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction.
Flydubai Chief Executive Ghaith Al Ghaith said in his first public comments on the incident that an official investigation was underway with the airline’s support.

“It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts,” Al Ghaith said in a written statement, while acknowledging that there were “many questions” surrounding what happened on flight FZ1073.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that Israel was investigating whether the co-pilot had acted under anyone’s direction.

extraction.body: TEL AVIV — Early indications suggest the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and trying to seize control of an Israel-bound plane acted alone, rather than as part of a larger organization or on behalf of a foreign government, multiple U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official told NBC News. The U.S. officials cautioned that the investigation into Wednesday’s midair attack remains at an early stage. “The assessment is that he operated alone. Right now, it looks like a case of ‘lone wolf’ terrorism inspired by content found online,” said Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official in the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency. “We still need to wait for the final investigation results to determine whether an organization or a state is behind it,” he added. Emirati authorities, who are leading the investigation, said Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash ax and attempted to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls in an attempted terrorist attack. The flight was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted when crew members and passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials. NBC News has identified the suspect as Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, based on information from multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East. Authorities have not released his identity. UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said Saturday that investigators were working to establish the incident’s “full circumstances, motives, and any links.” The preliminary assessment comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that investigators were examining whether the attacker had been sent by someone. President Donald Trump also raised the possibility of Iranian involvement Thursday, threatening renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack. A senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation previously told NBC News there were no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack. The flight captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar , said Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi that he had been severely injured and could sense the aircraft descending before he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene. “I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Raf Sanchez and Paul Goldman reported from Tel Aviv and Tom Winter from New York.

extraction.body: President Donald Trump announced a new "Super Intelligence Force" in a post on Truth Social Sunday, just days after signing an executive order renaming Artificial Intelligence. Trump says the force will "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," by coordinating the federal government's efforts. "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies," Trump said on Truth Social. He said the force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor will all serve as vice chairs. Clayton spoke with The Wall Street Journal about the force, saying, "The president asked that a group be put together." He said the panel has been tasked with reporting on the risks and opportunities AI poses within 120 days, and emphasized the U.S. government's desire to lead the industry, saying "the risk of not being first is high." According to The Journal, the force will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms, checking them for breaches, hacks and other incidents and issues. The Journal says in addition to Clayton and the vice chairs, Super Intelligence Force members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Super Intelligence vs AI The force is just the latest effort Trump has made, using the term superintelligence rather than artificial intelligence. During a UN General Assembly meeting last month, Trump said the word artificial "makes it sound fake, and it is not fake, it's actually amazing." Since then, he's signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to officially rebrand AI as "super intelligence" in federal communications.

(CNN) — President Donald Trump on Sunday announced the leadership and duties of a “Super Intelligence Force,” which he said will “ensure that America continues to lead the world” when it comes to artificial intelligence.
Trump announced last month that he was planning to create an “AI Force” and name an AI czar as the government faces growing calls to impose guardrails on the technology’s rapid development.
“I’m seeing tremendous self-policing, and they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters.
“These models are very complex and, again, I believe they’re going to be used for the good.”

The group signed a new commitment aimed at better “self-policing” their companies’ AI models, arguing that the light-touch approach represents the best way to balance safety concerns with the president’s desire to accelerate a technology he’s dubbed “Super Intelligence.”

The president said in his announcement on Truth Social that the task force will “protect the interests” and “improve the lives” of Americans. He said it will coordinate the government’s engagement with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, infrastructure providers and AI companies. The group will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor. The task force will report to Trump and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, the president said. Trump announced last month that he was planning to create an “AI Force” and name an AI czar as the government faces growing calls to impose guardrails on the technology’s rapid development. CNN reported Friday that Trump was expected to tap Clayton to lead the group. The announcement detailing the task force comes in the wake of episodes that have raised widespread safety concerns tied to AI, including AI agents going rogue and attempting to hack into federal databases. The president has made clear that he considers outpacing China and preserving AI-driven economic gains a higher priority than addressing growing public concerns, and previously referred to fears over AI as being a “hoax.” His support for the technology comes amid widespread frustrations over the data centers used to support it, which are shaking up midterm races. The president hosted top AI executives at the White House last week. The group signed a new commitment aimed at better “self-policing” their companies’ AI models, arguing that the light-touch approach represents the best way to balance safety concerns with the president’s desire to accelerate a technology he’s dubbed “Super Intelligence.” “I’m seeing tremendous self-policing, and they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters. “These models are very complex and, again, I believe they’re going to be used for the good.” When asked about AI during his confirmation hearing to lead the US intelligence community, Clayton said the technology is a “game changer.” “When something’s both an opportunity and a threat, you better get your arms around it,” Clayton said. extraction.body: If the future of AI has you worried, there's no need to fret now because the Super Intelligence Force is here. At least, that's what President Donald Trump wants Americans to think. Trump has gone so far to rebrand the term "artificial intelligence" with the creation of his new task force meant to maintain US' pole position in the industry. To lead the task force, Trump tapped Jay Clayton, the country's director of national intelligence. "The Super Intelligence Force is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post. The president detailed that the newly-formed group would work with consumers, public interest groups, religious organizations, critical infrastructure providers and "super intelligence companies." As first reported by The Wall Street Journal , the Super Intelligence Force already has its first task, which is to create a report on the risks and opportunities related to AI within 120 days. Along with Clayton, Trump also tapped Andrew Ferguson, chair of the Federal Trade Commission; Emil Michael, the Department of Defense's under secretary of war for research and engineering and chief technology officer; and Scott Kupor, the Office of Personnel Management's director. Trump said that the group will report to him and his chief of staff, Susie Wiles. The creation and staffing of the Super Intelligence Force comes a couple of weeks after Trump announced that he would create a new " AI Force ." Around the same time, the president also polled his followers on Truth Social about rebranding the term artificial intelligence. Now that the Super Intelligence Force is official, the task force will eventually share the recommendations for the federal government's responsibilities related to AI, during the current climate where many company CEOs have been calling for a development slowdown . (CNN) — President Donald Trump on Sunday announced the leadership and duties of a “Super Intelligence Force,” which he said will “ensure that America continues to lead the world” when it comes to artificial intelligence.
Trump announced last month that he was planning to create an “AI Force” and name an AI czar as the government faces growing calls to impose guardrails on the technology’s rapid development.
“I’m seeing tremendous self-policing, and they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters.
“These models are very complex and, again, I believe they’re going to be used for the good.”

The group signed a new commitment aimed at better “self-policing” their companies’ AI models, arguing that the light-touch approach represents the best way to balance safety concerns with the president’s desire to accelerate a technology he’s dubbed “Super Intelligence.”

extraction.body: President Donald Trump announced a new "Super Intelligence Force" in a post on Truth Social Sunday, just days after signing an executive order renaming Artificial Intelligence. Trump says the force will "ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," by coordinating the federal government's efforts. "The Super Intelligence Force will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies," Trump said on Truth Social. He said the force will be led by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton. Chairman of the Federal Trade Commission Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael, and Director of the Office of Personnel Management Scott Kupor will all serve as vice chairs. Clayton spoke with The Wall Street Journal about the force, saying, "The president asked that a group be put together." He said the panel has been tasked with reporting on the risks and opportunities AI poses within 120 days, and emphasized the U.S. government's desire to lead the industry, saying "the risk of not being first is high." According to The Journal, the force will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms, checking them for breaches, hacks and other incidents and issues. The Journal says in addition to Clayton and the vice chairs, Super Intelligence Force members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. Super Intelligence vs AI The force is just the latest effort Trump has made, using the term superintelligence rather than artificial intelligence. During a UN General Assembly meeting last month, Trump said the word artificial "makes it sound fake, and it is not fake, it's actually amazing." Since then, he's signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to officially rebrand AI as "super intelligence" in federal communications.
